exemplar: GUAVA (arXiv 2606.18363): Distilling Frontier VLMs into a Compact Agent through a Robotic Manipulation Harness
identification: Title: "Guava: Distilling Frontier VLMs into a Compact Agent through a Robotic Manipulation Harness". Authors: Haowen Liu*, Xirui Li*, Shaoxiong Yao*, Peng Shi, Tianyi Zhou, Jia-Bin Huang, Furong Huang, Jiayuan Mao (UMD, UIUC, U Waterloo, MBZUAI, UPenn, Amazon FAR). arXiv 2606.18363 (cs.RO). v1 (June 2026) had a different title, "Guava: An Effective and Universal Harness for Embodied Manipulation", so it was first framed as a harness paper. v3 (around Sept 2026) is framed as distillation. Links: project page https://guava-harness.github.io/ (source read via raw.githubusercontent), code https://github.com/hdacnw/guava-release (README, teacher system prompt and SFT prompt read), model at HF AIcell/guava-v13b-qwen3.5-4b. Robot: simulation is robosuite/MuJoCo; real robot is a Franka arm. Found while searching, and relevant to the user's question (b): "Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots" (arXiv 2609.10522, NUS Show Lab, Sept 2026) is almost certainly the "show harness" the user means. Its repo also announces a competing survey/awesome-list, showlab/Awesome-Multimodal-Embodied-Agent ("Agent + Robot landscape from computer-use to robot-use"), which the survey needs to differentiate from. ENPIRE is arXiv 2606.19980 ("ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World", NVIDIA GEAR + CMU + UC Berkeley). Code-as-Monitor is arXiv 2412.04455 (CVPR 2025). Other harness-family items seen in search: CaP-X 2603.22435 (ICML 2026; GUAVA compares to its CaP-Agent0), Harness Engineering for Physical AI 2606.09416, HarnessPAI 2609.29166, World Action Agent 2609.29964, EmbodiedSkills 2609.01281, Tool-Aligned VLA 2605.13119, FAEA 2601.20334, ALRM 2601.19510.
mechanism:
HARNESS (shared by teacher and student): a single-action ReAct loop. Each turn the model receives an RGB image (frontview, or sideview for shell game), numeric gripper state ([x,y,z], [roll,pitch,yaw], opening %), the text returned by the last tool, and the interaction history. It outputs a short public rationale in <think>…</think> plus exactly ONE JSON tool call, or ends with "Task complete." / "Task failed." Success is decided from observations only; there is no hidden success signal. The tools form a semantic, object-referenced skill API in a table-aligned metric frame:
- grasp(target): SAM3 segmentation, PCA grasp alignment, descend and close; returns "grasped" or "closed"
- align(target, top|left|right|front|back, clearance small 6cm | medium 10cm | large 20cm)
- get_position and get_position_and_size
- move([x,y,z]), rotate(angle, axis), close_gripper, release, home_pose
GraspGen is optional. The tools handle all physical-frame conversion and motion, so the VLM never outputs joint or torque commands.

Interface ablation (success %, GPT-5.4 / Qwen3.5-4B base):
| Harness variant | GPT-5.4 | Qwen3.5-4B |
|---|---|---|
| Full | 88.6 | 22.9 |
| Image-only | 56.2 | 3.8 |
| Image + gripper state | 77.1 | 10.5 |
| Low-level tools (end-effector pose + gripper width) | 73.3 | 4.8 |
| Multi-action replanning (program of tool calls) | 82.9 | 13.3 |
The interface matters more for the small model than for the frontier model.

TEACHER LOOP: GPT-5.4 (via OpenRouter, with a long data-generation prompt) runs the harness in randomized MuJoCo scenes and produces about 2,268 trajectories. v1 reported 1,191 successful episodes from 237 task prompts. Perturbation branching restores saved simulator and controller state at chosen turns, keeps the parent history, and injects a deviation: grasp_failure, wrong_object, drop_during_transport, object_moved_align, wrong_approach_side or wrong_orientation. Only successful recovery continuations are kept. Outcome labels go through automated consistency checks and human visual review. Evaluation-only tasks are filtered out.

DISTILLATION TARGET: full-parameter SFT of Qwen3.5-4B (ms-swift, ZeRO-3, 8 GPUs) on the teacher's interleaved reasoning and tool calls, conditioned on observations and execution feedback, using a short SFT prompt. This is behaviour cloning of the whole agent loop, not of motor actions. Optional online GRPO in the same harness (binary task reward, length penalty) raises shell game from 63.3 to 90.0 and red-objects-in-basket from 80.0 to 86.7.

DEPLOYMENT: Guava-4B is served locally with vLLM on one RTX 5090 inside the same harness, with no real-world fine-tuning.
- Real Franka, 9 tasks × 10 trials: 90.0% (GPT-5.4 93.3%, base model 28.9%).
- Simulation, 15 tasks × 30 trials: 87.1% (GPT-5.4 90.4%, base 22.2%).
- Unseen tasks: 90.8% with perturbation data vs 77.1% without.
- LIBERO-PRO (position / instruction perturbation): 0.41 / 0.41, vs π0.5 at 0.25 / 0.01 and CaP-Agent0 at 0.20 / 0.16.
- Efficiency: model-call latency 4.168 s to 0.587 s (7.1×); generated tokens per episode 2,389 to 795.
- It recovers from a real controller collision-reflex abort, a failure type absent from training.
Physical-robot driver code is not released. Path to physical action: VLM reasoning → semantic tool call → scripted perception and motion primitives → Cartesian controller. Agency stays at the tool-orchestration level throughout.
placement_challenge:
A naive "where does agency live" axis files GUAVA under (1) external orchestration, because Guava-4B calls grasp/align tools. That is accurate at deployment but misses the contribution: a training-time transfer between two agents through a shared interface. The authors themselves moved it between categories: v1 was a harness paper (inference-time agent design), v3 is a distillation paper. A single-locus label therefore conflates three independent questions:
- (A) LEVEL: where in the control stack the deliberative loop sits — over tools/skills; a hierarchical high-level module; inside the policy; across agents; or outside the control loop entirely (developer/researcher, e.g. ENPIRE).
- (B) PHASE: when the loop runs — inference, data/training, or development.
- (C) CARRIER: what runs it — frontier API vs compact local model.
GUAVA needs two further axes:
- (D) INTERFACE/ACTION ABSTRACTION: semantic tools vs code API vs poses/waypoints vs action tokens. GUAVA's ablation shows this decides whether a 4B model can be agentic at all. Show-Harness shows that "agent calling tools" and "VLA emitting tokens" lie on one continuum set by action-unit granularity.
- (E) TRANSFER TYPE: what crosses from the agentic process into the deployed system:
  - none: the agent IS the runtime system
  - agent→agent behaviour on the same interface (GUAVA, LocalNav, BLAZER, Octopus)
  - agent→policy behaviour on a different, lower interface; the loop collapses but implicit retry/recovery survives (Scaling-Up, EmbodiedSWE)
  - labels/reasoning (ECoT, CAST)
  - tasks/rewards/environments (GenSim, RoboGen)
  - code/policy edits (ENPIRE)
Clean placement of GUAVA: Level = orchestration; Phase = training → inference; Carrier = frontier → compact; Interface = semantic tools (identical for teacher and student); Transfer = same-interface agent-to-agent distillation; deployed system is agentic.
A principled scope rule follows. A work counts as agentic embodiment if a closed-loop, multi-step, feedback-conditioned foundation-model agent is causally upstream of physical action in at least one phase. It is core when the paper's contribution concerns that loop: its interface, feedback, verification or recovery, or its transfer into the deployed system. One-shot LLM annotation or relabeling without an interaction loop is a principled borderline/exclusion ("foundation model as annotator", not "agent").

exemplar: NVIDIA GEAR ENPIRE (ENvironment, Policy Improvement, Rollout, Evolution): coding agents autonomously run real-robot policy research on a robot fleet
identification: "ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World", arXiv 2606.19980 (submitted 2026-06-18, primary class cs.AI). Authors: Wenli Xiao, Jia Xie, Tonghe Zhang, Haotian Lin, Letian "Max" Fu, Haoru Xue, Jalen Lu, Yi Yang, Cunxi Dai, Zi Wang, Jimmy Wu, Guanzhi Wang, S. Shankar Sastry, Ken Goldberg, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Yuke Zhu, Guanya Shi. Affiliations: NVIDIA GEAR Lab, CMU, UC Berkeley. Project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/enpire/ . Code: https://github.com/NVlabs/ENPIRE (Apache-2.0). I read README.md, AGENTS.md, enpire/policy/autoresearch_instruction.md, enpire/env/docs/NEW_TASK.md and the PLD runtime README through raw.githubusercontent. arXiv and the project page were blocked, so paper-level numbers come from search snippets. The paper compares three coding agents: Codex (GPT-5.5), Claude Code (Opus 4.7) and Kimi Code (Kimi K2.6). Fleets have 1, 4 or 8 robots, and the code points to YAM arms. Tasks: Push-T, pin-box organization/insertion, GPU insertion into a motherboard, and zip-tie fastening/cutting. Reported success reaches 99% (one summary says "pass@8"). Fleet efficiency is measured with two metrics, Mean Robot Utilization (MRU) and Mean Token Utilization (MTU). Press coverage says token cost grows faster than fleet size. User-named neighbour cases I also resolved: "show harness" is Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots (arXiv 2609.10522, Show Lab NUS). "Harness VLA" is Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents (arXiv 2607.08448). GUAVA is listed as "Guava: Distilling Frontier VLMs into a Compact Agent through a Robotic Manipulation Harness" (arXiv 2606.18363).
mechanism:
AGENT: general-purpose frontier coding agents (Codex/Claude Code/Kimi Code CLIs), up to 8 running in parallel, one per robot station or experiment branch. They read AGENTS.md and an "auto-research contract" and work through a CLI (uv run enpire ...) plus a small tool registry: control.get_state, control.set_gripper, planning.freespace, vision.detect, vision.segment, vlm.query.

TWO PHASES. (1) Environment construction, with humans in the loop. Agents use tool calls and human feedback to write and validate the safety boundaries, an automatic physical reset (reset.py, CaP scripts) and an outcome verifier (verify.py: visual, contact or geometric score; VLM-based reward evaluation). These are optimized offline and then frozen as immutable APIs. (2) Fully autonomous "physical autoresearch". Each iteration follows the contract: record one falsifiable hypothesis; make the smallest policy-side change; run unit tests and offline eval; run only the approved number of real trials; inspect result.json, event logs, metrics and video; keep the change only if it passes the success and regression gates, otherwise git-revert. The Evolution module has agents analyze failures, consult literature, and edit training infrastructure and algorithm code. Across the fleet, a decentralized team tests training recipes asynchronously and shares or abandons ideas by average success rate ("evolutionary hypothesis selection").

WHAT THE AGENTS EDIT (mutable surface): CaP task programs (cap/saved_scripts/<task>/main.py), the skill library (skill_library/*.py: tool parameters and heuristics such as freespace_move, nudge, segment_object, sample_grasp_pose_2d), Hydra config overrides, and for neural tasks the policy/training code under enpire/policy/pld/ (a JAX actor/learner trained online, SERL/HIL-SERL style) plus reward configuration. They also launch and supervise the learner/actor and pause/resume robot control with explicit --confirm-control.

FORBIDDEN (immutable contract): reset.py, verify.py and the verifier threshold, robot-side reward/event code, the score implementation, safety and workspace limits, e-stop hooks, eval seeds, the artifact schema, and the contract file itself. Real motion needs station/calibration preflight and operator motion authorization. Policy code may not read privileged state or redefine success. The docs are slightly inconsistent here: NEW_TASK.md lets the agent edit "reward configuration" for PLD tasks, while the contract makes the score and robot-side reward read-only. So reward shaping is mutable but the success metric is not.

HOW OUTPUTS REACH ACTUATORS: in phase 2 the LLM never emits motor commands. It emits code diffs and CLI commands. These either run a deterministic CaP Python program over the skill library (Push-T: heuristic, no neural net) or start online RL that trains a neural actor, which then drives the arm (pin, GPU, zip-tie). The press summary describes the loop as scene reset → literature review → skill practice → low-level control iteration → policy training → VLM self-verification → repeat.

IS THE DEPLOYED POLICY AGENTIC? No. The final artifact is a static CaP program or a trained JAX neural policy. The agency was in the process that produced it, not in the product. The only residual hook is that CaP scripts could call vlm.query.
placement_challenge:
A naive "where does agency live" axis assumes a single artifact, the deployed robot system, and asks which component inside its control stack does the reasoning. ENPIRE has frontier multi-agent agency, but it is entirely outside the deployed system. Labelling it "multi-agent" would wrongly suggest robots collaborating at runtime. "External orchestration" is also wrong, because the agents never sequence skills during an episode. "Internalized" is wrong too: the RL policy has no reasoning. The other user cases break the same axis in different ways. GUAVA has frontier agency at data-generation time and compact agency at deployment. Code-as-Monitor has agency that persists at runtime but only as a verifier, not as the actor. Harness VLA and Show-Harness keep the agent at runtime as the controller and wrap a frozen VLA or semantic action interpreter as a tool.

PROPOSED FIX: replace the single locus with three coordinates.
(1) LOOP LEVEL: which feedback loop does the agent close, relative to the target policy (the thing that ultimately moves the body)?
- L0 control: ms, actions.
- L1 episode/task: seconds to minutes; planning, skill calls, monitoring, recovery.
- L2 learning: hours; data, reward, curriculum, success labels, training runs.
- L3 design/research: days; algorithms, infrastructure, environments, harnesses, bodies.
(2) ARTIFACT CHANNEL: what the agent emits and how it reaches actuators. In order: direct actions → tool/skill calls → executable policy code → training signals (reward/data/curriculum/verifier) → weights → harness/infrastructure/hardware.
(3) RESIDUAL AGENCY AT DEPLOYMENT:
- persistent (frontier agent stays in the loop)
- compressed (smaller distilled agent or single-turn agent, e.g. GUAVA, RHO, Recursive Harness Distillation)
- compiled (frozen program: ENPIRE CaP, Encore, generalized-TAMP programs)
- dissolved (neural weights: ENPIRE PLD, Eureka-trained policies)

Placements under these axes:
- ENPIRE: L3+L2, code and weights channel, compiled/dissolved.
- GUAVA: L2 data source for an L1 runtime agent, compressed.
- Code-as-Monitor: L1, verifier channel, persistent.
- Show-Harness / Harness VLA: L1, skill-call channel, persistent.

A fourth tag ENPIRE makes explicit is the PERMISSION SURFACE: which artifacts the agent may mutate versus which are frozen (reset, verifier, safety). This boundary is what makes outer-loop autonomy trustworthy against reward hacking, and it is a distinctive design dimension of the family.

exemplar: Code-as-Monitor (CaM): Constraint-aware Visual Programming for Reactive and Proactive Robotic Failure Detection (CVPR 2025)
identification: Title: "Code-as-Monitor: Constraint-aware Visual Programming for Reactive and Proactive Robotic Failure Detection". Authors: Enshen Zhou*, Qi Su*, Cheng Chi*, Zhizheng Zhang, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Lu Sheng, He Wang. Affiliations: Beihang University, Peking University, BAAI, Galbot. arXiv 2412.04455 (Dec 2024; v3 exists), CVPR 2025 (openaccess.thecvf.com Zhou_Code-as-Monitor_..._CVPR_2025_paper). Project page: https://zhoues.github.io/Code-as-Monitor/ (read from its source repo zhoues/zhoues.github.io). Headline result: 28.7% higher success rate and 31.8% less execution time under severe disturbances, compared with baselines (DoReMi, Inner Monologue among them) across three simulators (CLIPort-based tabletop and OmniGibson are named on the page) plus a real-world setup. On the "harness" terms the user mentioned: searches found a 2026 cluster that names itself "harness". Harness VLA (arXiv 2607.08448): an agentic planner calls a frozen VLA as a VLA_ACT primitive next to analytic primitives, and memory holds success rules and failure models. SafeHarness (2609.20822): a coding agent with an obstacle-aware harness that plans a route, verifies it, replans if needed, and only then executes. MotorMind (2609.38078): a "robot manipulation harness" where one frozen VLM plays Planner, Executor, Monitor, Verifier and Memory Manager. DynaHarness (2609.40306) and RegenHarness (2609.27612): governor harnesses that also self-improve. All of them put a monitor or verifier role inside the harness. A competing survey of this sub-area also exists: "No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies" (arXiv 2609.09250; ZJUSCL/Awesome-Robot-Verifier, 153 papers). It groups verifiers by judge source: human, rule/formal, learned/pretrained, or model-intrinsic. It lists CaM under "LLM-written reward and monitor code", next to Eureka, Text2Reward and ReKep.
mechanism: CaM has three VLM-centred modules that wrap an otherwise open-loop low-level policy. (1) Constraint Generator: from multi-view RGB(-D) observations, a VLM derives the next subgoal and a set of textual spatio-temporal constraints for it, such as "the lobster must stay inside the pan" or "the pan must stay level". (2) Painter: a trained constraint-aware segmentation model (ConSeg) produces instance-level and part-level masks across views. These are projected to 3D and, through heuristics, reduced to compact geometric "constraint elements" (points, lines, surfaces). The elements are drawn onto the multi-view images as visual prompts and are then tracked frame by frame with off-the-shelf trackers. (3) Monitor: GPT-4o is prompted with the subgoal's start frames, the annotated elements and the textual constraints. It writes Python "monitor code" that evaluates the constraints as geometric predicates over the tracked elements, such as distances, angles and containment. That code runs at every step without querying the VLM, which avoids the cost and the 3D-reasoning errors of per-step VLM queries (DoReMi) and the late detection of checking only at subgoal end (Inner Monologue). Reactive detection fires on a violation that has already happened, e.g. the lobster jumping out. Proactive detection fires on a trend toward a foreseeable violation, e.g. the pan tilting, or a moving glass during a grasp. Either way the code returns a failure reason, and that reason sends control back to the Constraint Generator/VLM to replan the next subgoal. This turns an open-loop policy into a closed-loop system for long-horizon tasks in cluttered, disturbed scenes. The agent never outputs motor actions. It outputs (a) subgoals and constraints and (b) an executable predicate program that gates the action stream and triggers replanning.
placement_challenge: Under a naive "where does agency live" axis, CaM goes into "external orchestration" next to Code as Policies and VoxPoser, because a frontier VLM writes code. That hides three facts. (1) Role: CaM's code never moves the robot. It is a predicate that decides when the robot's current behaviour is wrong. That is a supervisory or verifier role, distinct from controller, teacher, reward designer or developer. (2) Persistence: the agent is not in the per-frame loop. It runs per subgoal or per failure event and leaves behind a compiled artifact, the monitor program. Structurally this matches Eureka (reward code) and ENPIRE (code edits) at different timescales, and it resembles GUAVA's frontier-to-compact move, except that here agency is compiled into code rather than distilled into weights. (3) Coupling: CaM wraps an arbitrary, even open-loop, policy and needs no access to its internals, so it is orthogonal to whether the policy is a VLA, a skill library or a hierarchical system. Three axes place it cleanly. Role of the agent relative to the embodied policy: monitor/verifier. Timing and timescale of influence: inference, at event (subgoal or failure) granularity, with a compiled per-frame check. Form of the agent's output artifact: an executable predicate program, as opposed to actions, language corrections, scores, rewards, data or weights. Agency locus then becomes a fourth, descriptive attribute (frontier external, synthesis only), not the primary partition. A useful definitional point: the agentic component must close a loop that changes physical behaviour. CaM does, through replanning. A detector benchmarked offline does not.

exemplar: The user's "harness VLA" and "show harness" refer to "Harness VLA" (arXiv 2607.08448) and "Show-Harness" (arXiv 2609.10522). Both belong to a mid-to-late-2026 wave of embodied "harness" papers.
identification:
Most likely meaning, in order of confidence:
(1) "show harness" = "Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots". arXiv 2609.10522, Sep 2026. Authors: Yanzhe Chen*, Zechen Bai*, Zhijun Cao*, Wenzheng Zeng*, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Qiming Huang, Mike Zheng Shou (Show Lab, NUS). Code at github.com/showlab/Show-Harness; models and data at HF showlab/Show-Harness-VLMs and Show-Harness-Data. Confidence about 95%.
(2) "harness VLA" = "Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents". arXiv 2607.08448, submitted 9 Jul 2026 and revised 24 Sep 2026. It is the first paper of the RLinf team's RPent framework ("RPent: Agentic Infrastructure for the Physical World", github.com/RLinf/RPent). Confidence about 90%.
Second reading of "harness VLA": "AdaHVLA: Adaptive Harnesses for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Execution" (arXiv 2609.29204; Tang, Peng, Ding, Shen, T. Chen). Its repo is named "AdaHVLA-Adaptive_Harness_VLA". Confidence about 10%.
Wider "harness" wave the user may have in mind, all 2026: Robo-Harness K1 (2609.29389); RoboHarness/SOMA (2603.24060); RoboHarness memory-driven policy orchestration (2607.18060); HarnessPAI (2609.29166); RegenHarness (2609.27612); Recursive Harness Distillation (2609.33378); "Towards the Harness of Embodied Agents" (Thea, 2608.11246); "Harness Engineering for Physical AI: Robot Middleware Is the Harness Layer" (2606.09416); HarnessVLN (2609.15195); HARBOR (2606.08610); Guava (2606.18363).
Framing sources:
- Phillip Isola's essay "Robot-use agents" (web.mit.edu/phillipi/www/writing/robot-use-agents.html, 7 Sep 2026)
- Anthropic's "Claude Plays Robotics" (Aug 2026)
- The curated list github.com/visitworld123/Awesome-Robot-Use-Agent
- Closest competing survey: Show Lab's "Awesome Multimodal Embodied Agents: From Computer-Use to Robot-Use" (Sep 2026, 310 papers). It uses a PAPAV lens (Perceive, Anticipate, Plan, Act, Verify).
Note: the shared web-search budget ran out near the end. Gemini Robotics 1.5 is listed from memory. Some 2026 arXiv IDs come only from the fetched Awesome-Robot-Use-Agent README (a third-party list), not from a direct search.
mechanism:
HARNESS VLA (2607.08448):
- Agent: an agentic planner (a frontier coding or VLM agent such as Claude Code or Codex, or a custom planner inside RPent). It receives the task text, RGB-D and robot state, plus memory of earlier executions.
- What it outputs: it never emits low-level actions. It picks structured calls from a fixed primitive library:
  - VLA_ACT(instruction) runs a frozen VLA (pi0.5, RLDX-1 or LingBot-VLA) only for local, contact-rich phases.
  - Analytic primitives (MOVE_TO, ROTATE, SET_GRIPPER) handle perception-conditioned staging, transport, posture and release.
- Three duties are lifted out of the VLA into the planner: semantic re-grounding (rewriting the goal into instructions the VLA has seen), non-contact execution, and VLA re-staging (moving the robot back into the VLA's in-distribution start states).
- The loop closes per primitive call: execute, observe, consult memory, choose the next call.
- No fine-tuning. Reported gains: +38.6 pp on LIBERO-Pro, +25.4 pp on RoboCasa365, 58.4% on RoboTwin C2R.
- Path to physical action: agent tool call, then VLA or analytic controller, then robot. The VLA is demoted from "the policy" to "one motor primitive".

SHOW-HARNESS (2609.10522):
- Called an "embodied harness": a compact semantic action interface of discrete, incremental action units (keyboard-like gripper moves, rotations, open/close).
- Embodiment-specific interpreters turn each unit into robot motion deterministically. The VLM stays directly responsible for every fine-grained physical decision, with no VLA underneath.
- Plugins attach to loop stages, one boolean each:
  - Perception: multi-view guidance, proprioception.
  - Reasoning: subtask and situated planning, action chunking, adaptive step size, visual-prompt affordances.
  - Action: action history, failure recovery.
- Two modes share one interface:
  - Zero-shot: a closed frontier VLM runs the full plugin harness.
  - Fine-tuned: small VLMs (Qwen3.5 0.8B-9B, Gemma 4) get LoRA adapters trained on demonstrations. They emit one action token per step with no planner, so the "agent" becomes a compact policy over the harness's action vocabulary.
- GUMI (GUI Manipulation Interface) maps each action unit to a key or button. Humans, or GUI-driving agents, can then "play" the robot in a browser to collect training pairs without teleoperation hardware.
- The same vocabulary and prompts work across Franka, AgileX Piper (single and dual arm), ManiSkill, Isaac Lab and LIBERO. Only the interpreter changes.
- Claim: the right interface unlocks embodied capability from foundation VLMs without extra model capacity or embodiment-specific pretraining.

What both share: the "harness" is the scaffold between model and body, with five parts:
- Observation tools.
- Action vocabulary or tools.
- Loop and turn control.
- Memory/state.
- Verification and exit.
The papers treat the harness itself as the research object. Model weights are mostly held fixed.
placement_challenge:
Why "where does agency live" breaks:
- A naive axis assumes "the agent" and "the embodied policy" are fixed, separate boxes. The harness papers show the same harness can be filled by a frontier agent, a distilled 4B agent, or a 2B policy emitting single action tokens (Show-Harness; Guava; K1 fine-tuning 107 episodes).
- So "agent vs VLA" is not a property of the weights. It is a property of the loop and the interface.
- Harness VLA inverts the usual hierarchy: the VLA becomes a primitive inside the agent's toolset. Is that "external orchestration" or "dual-system"? Neither cleanly. It is a tool-level interface with an untrained VLA.
- Show-Harness zero-shot has no VLA at all. The agent is the policy at fine grain, so "external orchestration of skills" does not fit either.
- The fine-tuned mode looks like an "internalized VLA", yet it was obtained by distilling an agent loop through a harness.

The axis conflates at least four separable variables:
- (a) Loop position, i.e. which loop the agent closes and when:
  - In-the-loop: per-step or per-skill actuation within an episode.
  - On-the-loop: monitors, verifies or intervenes on a running policy (Code-as-Monitor, SOMA, CommitFlow, Recursive Harness Distillation).
  - Across-the-loop: rewrites harness, programs, memory or skills between episodes (HarnessPAI, AdaHVLA, RegenHarness).
  - Behind-the-loop: builds environments, rewards, data, training code (ENPIRE, HARBOR).
- (b) Action-interface granularity, i.e. what the agent emits that eventually reaches actuators: native commands (OpenRUA, AGP); semantic micro-actions (Show-Harness); parameterized skills (Guava, K1); learned-policy calls (Harness VLA, VLAs-as-Tools); programs (CaP-X, PyRUA-Lean, HarnessPAI); artifacts such as code, rewards and weights (ENPIRE).
- (c) Carrier of agency, i.e. which weights make the decision: frontier general model; distilled compact general model; embodied-specialized single model; or multiple agents.
- (d) Harness persistence at deployment: kept at runtime (Guava, Show-Harness, Harness VLA) or compiled away into programs or policy weights (HarnessPAI, the pi0.5 fine-tune, Show-Harness single-token mode).

A clean placement uses (a) loop position x (c) carrier as the philosophy view, and the harness anatomy (O, A, C, M, V) as the component view. Under this:
- Harness VLA = in-the-loop / frontier / VLA-call interface / harness kept.
- Show-Harness = in-the-loop / frontier then compact / micro-action interface / harness kept.
